clauses.text: These Directions shall be called the Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks Fraud Risk Management) Directions, 2026.

clauses.text: These Directions shall come into effect immediately upon issuance.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter I - Preliminary :: A. Short Title and Commencement

clauses.text: These Directions shall be applicable to Commercial Banks (hereinafter collectively referred to as 'banks' and individually as 'bank').
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter I - Preliminary :: B. Applicability

clauses.text: For the purpose of these Directions , 'Commercial Banks' is the term applied to banking  companies  (other  than  Small  Finance  Banks,  Payments  Banks,  and Local Area Banks), corresponding new banks, and the State Bank of India, as defined respectively under clauses (c), (da), and (nc) of Section 5 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949.

clauses.chapter_title: Chapter II - Governance and Oversight :: A. Governance Structure for Fraud Risk Management

clauses.chapter_title: Chapter II - Governance and Oversight :: A. Governance Structure for Fraud Risk Management

clauses.chapter_title: Chapter III - Early Detection of Frauds - Framework for Early Warning Signals and Red Flagging of Accounts :: A. Governance Structure

clauses.text: The EWS / RFA framework shall be subject to suitable validation in accordance with the directions of RMCB so as to ensure its integrity, robustness and consistency of the outcomes.

clauses.chapter_title: Chapter III - Early Detection of Frauds - Framework for Early Warning Signals and Red Flagging of Accounts :: A. Governance Structure

clauses.text: The bank shall set up a dedicated Data Analytics and MI Unit keeping in view its size, complexity, business mix and risk profile.

clauses.text: The bank shall report a n account, with an aggregate exposure of ₹3 crore and above, once red flagged in 'Red Flagged Account Return' on the Reserve Bank's CRILC platform within seven days of being red flagged.

clauses.text: The bank shall develop / strengthen its EWS system by identifying suitable indicators and parameterising them in its EWS system for monitoring other banking/non-credit related transactions.

clauses.chapter_title: Chapter III - Early Detection of Frauds - Framework for Early Warning Signals and Red Flagging of Accounts :: C. EWS Framework for Other Banking / Non-Credit Related Transactions

clauses.text: The bank shall strive to continuously upgrade the EWS system for enhancing its integrity and robustness, monitor other banking/non-credit related transactions efficiently and prevent fraudulent activities through the banking channel.

clauses.text: The design and specification of EWS system shall be robust and resilient to ensure that integrity of system is maintained, personal and financial data of customers are secure and transaction monitoring for prevention/detection of potential fraud is on real-time basis or with minimum time lag without compromising the effectiveness of the outcome of EWS system in prevention/detection of potential frauds.

clauses.text: In cases where Law Enforcement Agencies (LEAs) have suo moto initiated investigation involving a borrower account, the bank shall immediately red-flag the account and follow the usual process for classification of account as fraud and complete the same within the stipulated period as specified at Paragraph 31 above.

clauses.text: To ensure uniformity and consistency while reporting incidents of fraud to RBI through Fraud Monitoring Returns (FMRs) using online portal, the bank shall choose the most appropriate category from any one of the following:
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter VI - Reporting to Reserve Bank of India :: A. Reporting of Incidents of Fraud

clauses.text: Misappropriation of funds and criminal breach of trust;
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter VI - Reporting to Reserve Bank of India :: A. Reporting of Incidents of Fraud

clauses.text: Fraudulent encashment through forged instruments;
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter VI - Reporting to Reserve Bank of India :: A. Reporting of Incidents of Fraud

clauses.text: Manipulation of books of accounts or through fictitious accounts, and conversion of property;
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter VI - Reporting to Reserve Bank of India :: A. Reporting of Incidents of Fraud

clauses.text: Cheating by concealment of facts with the intention to deceive any person and cheating by impersonation;
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter VI - Reporting to Reserve Bank of India :: A. Reporting of Incidents of Fraud

clauses.text: Forgery with the intention to commit fraud by making any false documents / electronic records;
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter VI - Reporting to Reserve Bank of India :: A. Reporting of Incidents of Fraud

clauses.text: Wilful falsification, destruction, alteration, mutilations of any book, electronic record, paper, writing, valuable security or account with intent to defraud;
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter VI - Reporting to Reserve Bank of India :: A. Reporting of Incidents of Fraud

clauses.text: Fraudulent credit facilities extended for illegal gratification;
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter VI - Reporting to Reserve Bank of India :: A. Reporting of Incidents of Fraud

clauses.text: Cash shortages on account of frauds;
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter VI - Reporting to Reserve Bank of India :: A. Reporting of Incidents of Fraud

clauses.text: Fraudulent transactions involving foreign exchange;
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter VI - Reporting to Reserve Bank of India :: A. Reporting of Incidents of Fraud

clauses.text: Fraudulent electronic banking / digital payment related transactions committed on banks;
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter VI - Reporting to Reserve Bank of India :: A. Reporting of Incidents of Fraud

clauses.text: Other type of fraudulent activity not covered under any of the above.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter VI - Reporting to Reserve Bank of India :: A. Reporting of Incidents of Fraud

clauses.text: The bank shall put in place systems and procedures to ensure that the information available in Central Fraud Registry (CFR) is used for credit risk and fraud risk management effectively.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter VI - Reporting to Reserve Bank of India :: B. Central Fraud Registry

clauses.text: The bank is required to report payment system related disputed / suspected or attempted fraudulent transactions to Central Payments Fraud Information Registry (CPFIR), as required in terms of Circular Ref. CO.DPSS.OVRST. No.S1619/06-08-005/2022-23 dated December 26, 2022, maintained by RBI.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter VI - Reporting to Reserve Bank of India :: B. Central Fraud Registry

clauses.text: However, such transactions, if subsequently concluded as fraud committed on the bank, shall invariably be reported through FMR so as to be reflected in CFR.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter VI - Reporting to Reserve Bank of India :: B. Central Fraud Registry

clauses.text: The bank shall furnish FMR in individual fraud cases, irrespective of the amount involved, immediately, but not later than 14 days from the date of classification of an incident / account as fraud.

clauses.text: Incidents of fraud at overseas branches of Indian banks shall also be reported to the concerned overseas LEAs in accordance with the relevant laws / regulations of the host countries.

clauses.chapter_title: Chapter VI - Reporting to Reserve Bank of India :: C. Modalities of Reporting Incidents of Fraud

clauses.text: The group entities will have to comply with the principles of natural justice before declaration of fraud (refer to Paragraph 6).

clauses.chapter_title: Chapter VIII - Other Instructions :: A. Legal Audit of Title Documents in respect of Large Value Loan Accounts

clauses.text: The bank shall complete the investigation from fraud angle before transferring the loan account / credit facility to other lenders / Asset Reconstruction Companies (ARCs).
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter VIII - Other Instructions :: B. Treatment  of  Accounts  classified  as  Fraud  and  sold  to  other  Lenders  / Asset Reconstruction Companies 6

clauses.text: In cases where the bank concludes that a fraud has been perpetrated in the account, they shall report it to RBI before selling the accounts to other lenders / ARCs.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter VIII - Other Instructions :: B. Treatment  of  Accounts  classified  as  Fraud  and  sold  to  other  Lenders  / Asset Reconstruction Companies 6

clauses.text: In cases where accounts are sold to ARCs, the bank shall continue to report subsequent developments in such accounts to RBI, by obtaining requisite information periodically from the concerned ARCs.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter VIII - Other Instructions :: B. Treatment  of  Accounts  classified  as  Fraud  and  sold  to  other  Lenders  / Asset Reconstruction Companies 6

clauses.text: Internal  Audit  in  the  bank  shall  cover  controls  and  processes  involved  in prevention, detection, classification, monitoring, reporting, closure and withdrawal of fraud cases, as well as weaknesses observed in the critical processes in the fraud risk management framework of the bank, including delay in reporting, non-reporting, conduct of staff accountability examination and prudential provisioning.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter VIII - Other Instructions :: C. Role of Auditors

clauses.text: Reference is invited to the Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks - Transfer and Distribution of Credit Risk) Directions, 2025.
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter VIII - Other Instructions :: C. Role of Auditors

clauses.text: The bank shall report instances of theft, burglary, dacoity and robbery (including attempted cases), to Fraud Monitoring Group (FMG), Department of Supervision, Central Office, Reserve Bank of India, immediately (not later than seven days) from their occurrence, in the prescribed 'Return on Bank Robberies, Dacoities, Thefts and Burglaries (RBR)' format through e-mail (doscofrmc@rbi.org.in).
clauses.chapter_title: Chapter IX - Reporting Cases of Theft, Burglary, Dacoity and Robbery :: (full chapter)

clauses.text: The bank shall also submit a quarterly Return (RBR) on Bank Robberies, Dacoities, Thefts and Burglaries to RBI using online portal, covering all such cases during the quarter.
clauses.reason: clause describes a process or procedure with a customer-facing obligation

clauses.text: With  the  issue  of  these  Directions,  the  existing  directions,  instructions,  and guidelines relating to Fraud Risk Management as applicable to Commercial Banks stand repealed, as communicated vide circular no. DoS.CO.PPG.66/11.01.005/2026-27 dated July 31, 2026.
